title: Intermittent Demand Forecasting
interviewAnswer: Intermittent demand contains many zeros with irregular positive events. Standard smooth forecasts can be biased; Croston-style methods separately model demand size and inter-arrival intervals.
keyPoints: Zeros can be structural, not missing.
why: Intermittent Demand Forecasting appears frequently in data-science work because it connects mathematical assumptions to practical decisions, diagnostics and failure modes.
intuition: Zeros can be structural, not missing.
deepDive: Intermittent demand contains many zeros with irregular positive events. Standard smooth forecasts can be biased; Croston-style methods separately model demand size and inter-arrival intervals. Evaluate with business-relevant inventory metrics. Aggregate level can change intermittency. A strong practitioner separates the modeling assumption from the estimation procedure, checks diagnostics rather than trusting a single score, and explains what would make the method inappropriate.
workedExample: Forecast spare-part demand where most days have zero orders and occasional bursts occur.
commonMistakes: Applying the method without checking its assumptions or data-generating process.
Choosing it because it is familiar rather than comparing against an appropriate baseline.
followUps: What assumptions does Intermittent Demand Forecasting make?
How would you validate or debug Intermittent Demand Forecasting in practice?
production: In production, validate assumptions on real data, monitor the quantities that can drift, and keep a simple baseline so added complexity has a measurable reason to exist.
